notation: Each vector case runs one instruction on one wave with every lane active unless 'exec' is given. op is the canonical dotted name of the semantics . ins is that instruction at the decoded level , the machine's input, which bypasses any.s reader: {op, kind, operands, fields}, each operand {reg: [file, first, count]}, {lit: [32-bit pattern, text]} or {label: name}, with neg / abs when set; the registers are d = v1 (v[1:2] for 64 bits), x = v8, y = v10, z = v12 (pairs from there), scalar sources s20, s21, s22 (64-bit ones s[20:21], s[22:23]), a scalar destination s30 (s[30:31]); the lane mask is [vcc, 0, 2] at W = 64 (count W / 32; the cases run at W = 32). The in / old / mask_in values go into those registers. Lane l of the wave holds lane (l mod 16)'s inputs; 16 lanes are shown. in: per source x, y, z (in operand order after the destination) either 16 lane values, {sgpr: v} (a scalar register, the same in every lane), {literal: v}, or {lo, hi} (a 64-bit source as two dwords). old: the destination's dwords before. mask_in: the lane-mask source (carry-in, select) for lanes 0..15 (repeated every 16 lanes). out: d (and d2 for a second dword) per lane, and mask: the lane-mask result for lanes 0..15. fields: the instruction's fields. Scalar cases: in are the sources (64-bit sources as one value), scc_in, out d (absent: no destination) and scc. A destination starts as 0xa5a5a5a5 and other registers as the poison value 0x7fc17fc1.
